fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people?

questions.passage: Universal design suggests that design be as (A)[flexible / rigid] as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding (B)[adjustable / fixed] features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more (C)[common / unusual] types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① flexible(유연한)+adjustable(조절 가능한)+common(흔한): 유니버설 디자인은 다양한 요구를 수용하도록 '유연'해야 하고, 제품에 '조절 가능한' 기능을 더하며, 왼손잡이용 제품이 '흔한' 종류와 다르다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② rigid(뻣뻣한)는 '가능한 한 유연하게'라는 흐름과 정반대
❌ ③ fixed(고정된)는 '조절 가능한 기능을 더한다'는 설명과 반대
❌ ④ unusual(드문)은 특별한 제품이 '흔한' 종류와 다르다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: flexible=유연한, adjustable=조절 가능한, common=흔한

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is (A)[accessible / restricted] to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts (B)[eliminate / create] barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, (C)[automatic / manual] doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① restricted(제한된)는 '모두가 접근할 수 있게' 한다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② accessible(접근 가능한)+eliminate(없애다)+automatic(자동의): 환경이나 제품이 모두에게 '접근 가능'해야 하고, 연석 경사로가 장벽을 '없애며', '자동'문이 모두를 들어오게 한다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ create(만들다)는 장벽을 '없앤다'는 흐름과 정반대
❌ ④ manual(수동의)은 저절로 열리는 '자동'문 설명과 반대
det.tip: accessible=접근 가능한, eliminate=없애다, automatic=자동의

questions.passage: Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used (A)[efficiently / poorly] and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great (B)[challenge / relief] to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various (C)[clever / useless] opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① poorly(형편없이)는 '효율적으로' 쓰인다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② relief(안도)는 꽉 낀 뚜껑을 여는 것이 '큰 어려움'이라는 흐름과 반대
✅ ③ efficiently(효율적으로)+challenge(어려움)+clever(기발한): 제품이 '효율적으로' 쓰이고, 뚜껑 열기가 힘없는 사람에게 큰 '어려움'이 되며, 이를 돕는 '기발한' 장치가 고안됐다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ④ useless(쓸모없는)는 '기발한' 개봉 장치라는 설명과 반대
det.tip: efficiently=효율적으로, challenge=어려움, clever=기발한

det.korean: ④ resemble → differ: 왼손잡이용 제품이 흔한 종류와 어떻게 '다른지(differ)' 묻는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① mere: 'go beyond mere pretty looks'(그저 예쁜 겉모습을 넘어서)라는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ resemble(닮다) → differ(다르다): 'how they differ from the more common types'에서 왼손잡이용 제품이 흔한 종류와 '다른' 점을 묻는 것이므로 differ가 맞다. resemble은 정반대 ← 정답
det.tip: differ(다르다) ↔ resemble(닮다)

det.korean: ① harms → benefits: 레버형 손잡이가 바구니를 든 사람들에게 '이로움을 준다(benefits)'
det.analysis:
❌ ① harms(해를 끼치다) → benefits(이롭게 하다): 'which benefits people carrying baskets'에서 레버형 손잡이가 바구니를 든 사람에게 '이로움을 준다'는 뜻이므로 benefits가 맞다. harms는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ② critical: 'critical information is conveyed well'(중요한 정보가 잘 전달되는)이라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ written: 'not just through written language'(문자 언어를 통해서만이 아니라)라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ recognized: 'universally recognized restroom symbol'(보편적으로 인식되는 화장실 기호)이라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: benefits(이롭게 하다) ↔ harms(해를 끼치다)

det.analysis:
✅ ① presented: 'arrival times are ... presented on electronic boards'(전광판에 표시되는)라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② conceals(감추다) → indicates(나타내다): 'braille, which indicates the floor number'에서 점자가 층 번호를 '나타낸다'는 뜻이므로 indicates가 맞다. conceals는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ③ confirm: 'audio announcements confirm the selected floor'(선택된 층을 확인해 주는)라는 문맥에 적절

❌ ① device(장치): 특정 일을 위해 만든 도구
❌ ② symbol(기호): 무언가를 나타내는 표시
❌ ③ handle(손잡이): 문이나 물건을 잡는 부분
✅ ④ barrier(장벽): 움직임을 막거나 사람들이 무언가를 하거나 다다르지 못하게 하는 것 ← 정답
det.tip: without any barriers = 아무 장벽 없이 → barrier = 접근을 막는 것

questions.passage: This could involve __________ (provide) a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: provide(동사 원형) → providing(동명사): 동사 involve는 목적어로 동명사(-ing)를 취한다. 'involve providing(제공하는 것을 포함하다)'이 맞으므로 provide를 providing으로 바꿔야 한다. 뒤에 이어지는 'adding'과 형태가 같은 병렬이라는 점도 힌트다.
det.tip: involve + 동명사(-ing): involve providing(제공하는 것을 포함하다)

questions.passage: The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that __________ (accommodate) a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: accommodate(동사 원형) → accommodates: 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 'a universal design'으로 단수다. 관계절 안의 동사는 선행사의 수에 맞춰야 하므로 단수 주어에 맞는 3인칭 단수 현재형 accommodates로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: 관계대명사 that의 선행사(단수 a universal design) → 단수 동사 accommodates

questions.passage: Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities.  Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.  Information should be conveyed not just through __________ but also through universal symbols and audio cues.  For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.  For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements.  In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① written language(문자 언어): 정보는 '문자 언어'만이 아니라 보편적 기호와 소리 신호로도 전달되어야 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ② loud music(시끄러운 음악): 정보 전달 수단과 무관
❌ ③ bright colors(밝은 색): 뒤의 '기호·소리'와 대비되는 수단으로 어색함
❌ ④ physical touch(신체 접촉): 본문에서 다루지 않은 수단
det.tip: not just through written language but also through symbols and audio cues: 문자 언어뿐 아니라 기호와 소리로도

questions.passage: Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues.  For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language.  For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through __________.  In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor.  Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor.  As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① printed maps(인쇄된 지도): 시각·청각 장애인을 위한 소리 수단이 아님
✅ ② voice announcements(음성 안내): 도착 시간이 전광판에 표시될 뿐 아니라 '음성 안내'로도 알려진다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ hand signals(수신호): 앞의 '전광판'과 짝을 이루는 청각 수단이 아님
❌ ④ bright lights(밝은 조명): 소리로 알려 준다는 흐름과 맞지 않음
det.tip: not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements: 전광판뿐 아니라 음성 안내로도
